 Revised: Sep 30, 2026        Danuri / KPLO Spacecraft (Moon)             -155
                        https://www.kari.re.kr/eng/sub03_07_01.do

 BACKGROUND:
  The KPLO (Korea Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter) mission, renamed Danuri prior to
  launch, is South Korea's first lunar mission. It is developed and managed by 
  the Korea Aerospace Research Institute (KARI). 

 LAUNCH
  Nominal launch occurred 2022-Aug-4 @ 23:08 UTC on a Falcon-9 v1.2 (Block 5) 
  from Cape Canaveral (SLC-40).

  After launch, it was placed in a 300 km staging orbit around Earth to then 
  follow a ballistic lunar transfer to lunar orbit (BLT/WSB) via Earth-Sun L1,
  arriving at the Moon December 16, 2022 (UTC).

 MISSION GOALS:
  - nominal one year mission
  - image high interest and potential landing sites for later missions
  - investigate characteristics of lunar regolith
  - investigate characteristics of and map lunar resources including minerals
     and rare elements
  - measure the strength of the lunar magnetic field
  - image permanently shadowed regions to detect seasonal changes, search 
     for frost and ice deposits, and measure terrain inside the crater 
     including boulder distribution

 SCIENCE INSTRUMENTS
  KPLO carries six instuments, five from KARI and one from NASA:

   * Lunar Terrain Imager (LUTI) will take < 5m high-resolution images of 
      potential landing sites for later missions as well as high-interest sites
   * Wide-Angle Polarimetric Camera (PolCam) will acquire polarimetric images
      of the lunar surface (except for polar regions) with medium resolution
   * KPLO Magnetometer (KMAG) will measure the magnetic strength of the lunar 
      environment up to ~100 km above the lunar surface
   * KPLO Gamma Ray Spectrometer (KGRS)
   * Disruption Tolerant Network experiment (DTNPL) will test space 
      communications based on disruption-tolerant network technology
   * NASA's ShadowCam is a high-resolution camera based on the Lunar 
      Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) Narrow Angle Camera, but 800 times more 
      sensitive, and will study permanently shadowed regions (PSRs)

 SPACECRAFT PHYSICAL CHARACTERISTICS:
   * Dimensions (bus)    : 1.82m  x 2.14m x 2.29m
   * Mass                : 678 kg
   * Power               : 760 W, two deployable solar panels
   * Propulsion          : 4x30N and 4x5N monopropellant thrusters

 SPACECRAFT TRAJECTORY:
  Post-launch trajectory segments from KARI, concatenated and then merged with 
  a longer-term prediction. 

  Tag-up w/data through September 29, prediction thereafter.

TIME

  Barycentric Dynamical Time ("TDB" or T_eph) output was requested. This
continuous coordinate time is equivalent to the relativistic proper time
of a clock at rest in a reference frame co-moving with the solar system
barycenter but outside the system's gravity well. It is the independent
variable in the solar system relativistic equations of motion.

  TDB runs at a uniform rate of one SI second per second and is independent
of irregularities in Earth's rotation.
 
CALENDAR SYSTEM

  Mixed calendar mode was active such that calendar dates after AD 1582-Oct-15
(if any) are in the modern Gregorian system. Dates prior to 1582-Oct-5 (if any)
are in the Julian calendar system, which is automatically extended for dates
prior to its adoption on 45-Jan-1 BC.  The Julian calendar is useful for
matching historical dates. The Gregorian calendar more accurately corresponds
to the Earth's orbital motion and seasons. A "Gregorian-only" calendar mode is
available if such physical events are the primary interest.

REFERENCE FRAME AND COORDINATES

  Ecliptic at the standard reference epoch

    Reference epoch: J2000.0
    X-Y plane: adopted Earth orbital plane at the reference epoch
               Note: IAU76 obliquity of 84381.448 arcseconds wrt ICRF X-Y plane
    X-axis   : ICRF
    Z-axis   : perpendicular to the X-Y plane in the directional (+ or -) sense
               of Earth's north pole at the reference epoch.

  Symbol meaning:

    JDTDB    Julian Day Number, Barycentric Dynamical Time
      EC     Eccentricity, e
      QR     Periapsis distance, q (km)
      IN     Inclination w.r.t X-Y plane, i (degrees)
      OM     Longitude of Ascending Node, OMEGA, (degrees)
      W      Argument of Perifocus, w (degrees)
      Tp     Time of periapsis (Julian Day Number)
      N      Mean motion, n (degrees/sec)
      MA     Mean anomaly, M (degrees)
      TA     True anomaly, nu (degrees)
      A      Semi-major axis, a (km)
      AD     Apoapsis distance (km)
      PR     Sidereal orbit period (sec)

ABERRATIONS AND CORRECTIONS

 Geometric osculating elements have NO corrections or aberrations applied.
